messages:
support-ops: heads up — onboarding customer 'CedarMaps' opened an escalation. their p95/p99 on text-generation endpoints spiked ~3x starting 08:10 UTC. they report 500s and long tails for a subset of requests. attaching request ids and sample traces below. cc @alex @maria :alarm_clock:

alex: got it. do we have a link to the error patterns or a sample request-id? can you paste the failing request id(s)?

support-ops: sample IDs: `req_8a7f3c`, `req_b1d2e4`, `req_c0ffee`. Here are snippets from their client: 502/504s and a few 200s with 10-20s latencies. They say it started after a mid-morning traffic bump (~3x burst).

maria: quick check — which Dedicated pool are they on?

support-ops: pool: `dedicated-northstar-42` (customer-configured pool, min=2, max=12, autoscale policy=burst with attach-concurrency=3).

jordan: 3x burst + low min size + attach concurrency=3 smells like scale-up contention and cold-GPU handshakes. can we pull autoscaler and provisioner logs from the window? @deploy-bot any recent infra jobs?

deploy-bot: noticed a cleanup cron at 07:50 that terminated 6 idle instances in `dedicated-northstar-42` to hit resource efficiency targets. job id: `cleanup-2026-03-12-0750`

alex: nice — that explains low headroom. can someone grep the autoscaler logs 08:05-08:20 for `scale-up`, `attach`, `throttle`?

emily: grabbing logs now. here are relevant lines:

```
2026-03-12T08:06:12Z autoscaler INFO request=req_8a7f3c action=scale-up attempt=1 note="provisioning queued"
2026-03-12T08:06:13Z provisioner WARN instance_start id=i-0abc attach_time_est=19.2s
2026-03-12T08:06:14Z autoscaler ERROR reason=rate-limited backoff_ms=30000 policy=global-provisioner-throttle
2026-03-12T08:06:45Z provisioner INFO instance_ready id=i-0abc warmup_kv=false
2026-03-12T08:07:48Z attach ERROR id=i-0abc reason=handshake_timeout
2026-03-12T08:07:50Z autoscaler INFO request=req_b1d2e4 action=scale-up attempt=2 note="fallback queued"
2026-03-12T08:08:01Z serve INFO request=req_b1d2e4 status=200 latency_ms=12745
2026-03-12T08:09:03Z autoscaler INFO request=req_c0ffee action=route-to-fallback model=smaller-3b
```

jordan: attach handshake_timeout at 08:07 — that's the cold GPU not finishing the agent handshake before client timeout. also see `rate-limited` from autoscaler; looks like a global provisioner throttle kicked in.

maria: do we have provisioner capacity metrics? were there cluster-wide provisioning spikes at the same time?

emily: yes, in the region there was a simultaneous burst from 5 other customers between 08:05-08:09. our provisioner QPS hit the configured soft-limit (100 req/min) and the global backoff started.

alex: so root cause chain: cleanup reduced idle headroom earlier -> burst across customers -> autoscaler requests queued -> global provisioner throttle -> slow/failed attach handshakes -> elevated p95/p99 for CedarMaps. makes sense.

support-ops: customer wants immediate mitigation; they flagged this as P1. what can we do right now?

jordan: immediate mitigations (short-term):
- temporarily increase pool min for dedicated-northstar-42 to 6 to provide spare capacity.
- temporarily raise global provisioner soft-limit for region X by 30% to avoid backoff.
- enable model fallback (already triggered for some reqs) and increase fallback ratio to route more traffic to smaller 3B
- add pre-warm flag on their heavy routes (if supported) to keep KV cache warm on the spawned instances

maria: agreed. I'll run the pool min bump and request a regional soft-limit increase. Alex — can you push a policy tweak to allow emergency-provisioning for customers flagged P1?

alex: on it. patching autoscaler policy `emergency_headroom` to 4 for ops-flagged customers. running command now:

```
./rctl set-pool-min --pool dedicated-northstar-42 --min 6 --reason "P1 CedarMaps surge"
./provisionerapi update-soft-limit --region us-west-2 --delta +30
```
deploy-bot: pool min update succeeded: `dedicated-northstar-42` min=6 (applied by alex)

sre-bot: provisioner soft-limit request queued. expected propagation 45s.

emily: post-mitigation metrics — p95 dropped from ~3.1s to 420ms within ~90s after pool min bump and soft-limit change. p99 still a bit high but trending down.

support-ops: CedarMaps confirms improved experience, thanks. they want a writeup of root cause and longer-term fixes.

jordan: long-term action items (RCA):
1) revisit cleanup cron thresholds — ensure min pool headroom never falls below 30% of burst capacity for customer pools with `burst` policy.
2) implement a per-customer emergency headroom toggle (ops + customer SSR) so we can pre-authorize higher min for critical customers.
3) improve provisioner elasticity — allow short-term temporary quota bump automated when measuring cross-customer bursts (with circuit-breaker safeguards).
4) reduce attach handshake timeout by optimizing agent bootstrap (agent v2 has ~30% faster handshake; schedule rollout for dedicated pools).
5) surface a telemetry alert when global provisioner QPS > 80% to trigger automatic ramps or slowdown of cleanup jobs.

alex: also add an SRE playbook snippet for support-ops to run the 2-step mitigation with justifications and rollback commands. I'll draft.

maria: I'll own the RCA doc and timeline. targeted deliverables: RCA in 48h, mitigation runbook in 24h, agent upgrade plan in 2 weeks.

jordan: one more note — we saw `warmup_kv=false` on the new instance. KV warmup isn't automatic for some instance types. include a warmup job in the pre-provision flow.

emily: filing the incident in Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7623 (ticket created). tagging stakeholders: @product, @support, @infra.

support-ops: thanks team. customer is satisfied for now. please post the RCA link when ready. :thumbsup:

alex: posting interim notes to the incidents channel and will follow up with the runbook draft here.

maria: will add the cron config change to the infra repo and open PR referencing INF-7623.

emily: closing thread for now. will reopen if any regression. :lock:
